evals.prompt: Set up a /goal so /dev #42 runs autonomously until done. The project is a Gradle Android app; CLAUDE.md lists `./gradlew test` and `./gradlew detekt` as quality gates.
evals.expected_output: A single /goal condition derived from the repo, not a wrapper around the raw request
expectations: The condition names `./gradlew test` (resolved from CLAUDE.md), not a guessed command like `npm test`
The condition requires an exact evidence signal from command output (e.g. BUILD SUCCESSFUL / 0 failed) in the most recent turn
The condition requires review.json counts printed as text with "critical": 0
The stop clause is OR-joined into the condition ("— or stop after N turns"), not a separate sentence
A guardrail forbids modifying test files and requires `git diff --stat` as proof

evals.prompt: You are mid-run under /goal for issue #42. You just refactored the auth module after an earlier turn showed all tests passing. What do you do before ending the turn?
evals.expected_output: Re-run the test command and show fresh output
expectations: The tests are re-run in the current turn after the change
The reasoning notes that the evaluator discounts evidence that predates the last change

evals.prompt: You are on turn 25 of 25 under a /goal with the clause "— or stop after 25 turns, then summarize the blocker", and 2 tests still fail. What do you do?
evals.expected_output: Stop on this turn and print a blocker summary
expectations: No further fix attempts are made past the cap
A blocker summary is printed in the same turn (the stop branch only completes if the summary appears)
